text:
elaine: quick FYI — release/1.2 CI started failing on integration tests after the deps bump
elaine: looks like fastapi->starlette interaction changed behavior, error surfaces in our auth middleware
tim: ugh. stacktrace?
jordan: paste from CI logs:
```
File "/srv/app/middleware/auth.py", line 48, in __call__
  scope["user"] = await starlette.auth.get_current_user(request)
TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable
```
sam: interesting, root cause might be the starlette response changes in 0.24.0 that changed request.scope defaults
elaine: CVE check — I scanned for public advisories. No published CVE for starlette yet, but fastapi pinned to older ABI in some distros. security-bot: no CVE found for starlette 0.24.0
tim: still, this is a regression we need to triage with priority P1 for CI unblock
jordan: repro locally with poetry env. steps:
- poetry install
- tox -e integration
I can push a branch with the failing test
elaine: can you include the poetry.lock diff? maybe a transient wheel rebuilt changed manylinux tag
jordan: snip of lock diff:
```
- starlette = "^0.23.0"
+ starlette = "^0.24.0"
```
sam: we recently rotated KMS keys for staging yesterday — unrelated but putting on radar. Could also be RBAC middleware coupled with key lookup failing if kms-sdk exceptions bubble up differently with new deps
tim: @security-bot — can you run an audit for any kms-sdk breakage patterns in the commit range?
security-bot: running audit... (this can take a few mins)
elaine: short term plan: rollback starlette pin on release branch to 0.23.x to get CI green, then create a follow-up to test KMS/RBAC paths thoroughly
sam: agreed. Also add an integration that exercises encrypted config fetch + rbac role lookup
jordan: opening PR now: revert starlette bump + regen lock. Branch: patch/ci-unblock-starlette-revert
deploy-bot: deploy preview created for patch/ci-unblock-starlette-revert — preview URL: https://deploy.previews/redwood/patch-123
tim: after CI passes, security follow-up: we should do a deeper dependency review and check if any of our middleware exceptions could leak secrets when de-serializing request bodies
elaine: also add a note to the KMS rotation checklist: run integration against latest deps before rotation complete
security-bot: audit complete: found one callsite where kms.Client.get_key raises ClientError subclass that isn't caught in auth middleware. Flagged in GH issue #489
sam: ok I'll add try/except and explicit logging + SENTRY capture without secrets
jordan: CI green on revert branch. merging to release/1.2 now.
elaine: thanks all. follow-ups: (1) recreate bump in a feature branch and add new integration tests exercising RBAC+KMS; (2) add a short runbook entry so future KMS key rotations include a deps smoke test; (3) check transformers/tokenizers pinned extras in our build images (they pulled in a newer starlette via a transitive dep last week)
tim: making checklist items in the security backlog. :white_check_mark:
elaine: closing thread here — please add any additional context to GH #489 and link the runbook PR when ready
